title: Cookie Brownie with Icing or Filling

content.title: About
content.content: A cookie‑brownie is a soft, moist cookie that blends the rich chocolate flavor of a brownie with a crisp cookie base. The iced version is topped with a sweet chocolate or vanilla glaze, while the filled version contains a layer of cream, jam, or nut paste. It is popular as a tea‑time treat or a party snack.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The cookie‑brownie originated in the United States in the early 1920s as an experimental mash‑up of two beloved desserts.
There are more than ten filling varieties: caramel, cream cheese, nut butter, fruit jam, and others.
Glaze is often made from melted chocolate mixed with butter, giving it a glossy, smooth finish.
Brownie batter typically contains more cocoa and less sugar than standard cookie dough, resulting in a deeper flavor.
Cookie‑brownies are frequently included in DIY baking kits where consumers can add their own toppings.

items.title: Source of antioxidants
items.content: Cocoa in the brownie is rich in flavonoids, which help combat free radicals.

items.title: Quick energy
items.content: The product provides fast‑acting carbohydrates that replenish glycogen stores after exercise.

items.title: Contains magnesium
items.content: Magnesium from cocoa supports muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Provides iron
items.content: Dark chocolate contributes a modest amount of iron, beneficial for blood formation.

items.title: Fiber content
items.content: When whole‑grain flour is used in the dough, dietary fiber is increased, aiding digestion.

items.title: High sugar content
items.content: Glaze and fillings often contain a lot of sugar, which can contribute to weight gain if consumed in excess.

items.title: Dairy allergy
items.content: Glaze and many fillings are made with butter or cream, which may trigger reactions in people with lactose intolerance or milk allergy.

items.title: Caffeine and theobromine
items.content: Cocoa contains small amounts of theobromine, which can affect sleep in sensitive individuals.

items.title: Calorie dense
items.content: The combination of dough, glaze, and filling makes the product calorie‑dense, so portion control is advisable.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cookie‑brownies are easy to eat by hand as a snack, or they can be plated with a cup of tea or coffee. Slice them into bite‑size pieces, top with ice cream, whipped cream, or fresh berries for a more indulgent dessert.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days. For longer freshness (up to 2 weeks) keep refrigerated. Freeze in a sealed bag for month‑plus storage; thaw at room temperature before serving.
